'''Trent John Alexander-Arnold''' (born 7 October 1998), sometimes known mononymously as '''Trent''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Trent |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/futbol/primer-equipo-masculino/plantilla/trent-alexander-arnold |access-date=5 July 2025 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=12 June 2025 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold shirt number: Why ex-Liverpool man can't wear 66 at Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cg4v7nk3vw9o |access-date=5 July 2025 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] or [[midfielder]] for {{Spanish football updater|Real Madrid}} club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and the [[England national football team|England national team]].

Alexander-Arnold joined [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s [[Liverpool F.C. Reserves and Academy|academy]] in 2004 and captained the club across its youth levels. He made his senior debut in 2016, at age 18, and played in back-to-back [[UEFA Champions League]] finals in [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018]] and [[2019 UEFA Champions League final|2019]], winning the latter, and being named in the Champions League Squad of the Season. These appearances made him the youngest player to start in consecutive finals in the competition. In the same year, he won the [[2019 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] and the [[2019 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]]. In domestic football, Alexander-Arnold was named the 2019–20 [[PFA Young Player of the Year]] and the inaugural [[Premier League Young Player of the Season]], has thrice been named in the [[PFA Team of the Year]], and helped end Liverpool's [[2019–20 Liverpool F.C. season|30-year league title drought]] by winning the [[2019–20 Premier League]]. His success in 2020 led to his selection in the [[FIFPRO#FIFA FIFPRO Men's World 11|FIFA FIFPRO Men's World 11]]. In the 2021–22 season, he claimed a domestic cup double, winning the [[2021–22 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2021–22 FA Cup|FA Cup]]. In 2025, after helping Liverpool to [[2024-25 Premier League|their second Premier League title]], Alexander-Arnold joined La Liga club Real Madrid.

Alexander-Arnold has also represented England at various youth levels and made his senior debut in 2018. He has since featured at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]], where he became only the fourth teenager to start a match for England in the tournament, in the [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League]], where his nation finished in third place in the inaugural edition of the competition, and the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Liverpool===
====2016–17: Development and breakthrough====
[[File:Trent Alexander Arnold 2016.jpg|thumb|upright|Alexander-Arnold playing for [[Liverpool F.C. Reserves and Academy|Liverpool U18]] in 2016]]

Having previously taken part in Liverpool's pre-season tour of the United States, Alexander-Arnold made his professional debut on 25 October 2016, starting in a 2–1 victory over [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in the fourth round of the [[EFL Cup]]. He was [[Penalty card#Yellow card|booked]] in the first half for a foul on [[Ben Davies (footballer, born 1993)|Ben Davies]], which he later revealed could have ended in him being sent off, before being [[Substitute (association football)|substituted]] for first-choice right-back [[Nathaniel Clyne]] in the 68th minute.<ref name=JPA/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/liverpool/story/2960077/trent-alexander-arnold-hopeful-of-chance-in-liverpool-first-team |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold hopeful of chance in Liverpool first team |first=Glenn |last=Price |publisher=ESPN |date=28 September 2016 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311002359/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/liverpool/story/2960077/trent-alexander-arnold-hopeful-of-chance-in-liverpool-first-team |archive-date=11 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37686653 |title=Liverpool 2–1 Tottenham Hotspur |first=Luke |last=Reddy |website=BBC Sport |date=25 October 2016 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311002530/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37686653 |archive-date=11 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Despite the indiscretion, his performance earned a spot in the EFL Cup Team of the Round alongside teammate [[Daniel Sturridge]].<ref name = Uncle/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2016/october/team-of-the-round-a-stand-out-xi-from-efl-cup-round-four/ |title=Team of the Round: A stand-out XI from EFL Cup Round Four |publisher=English Football League |date=18 October 2016 |access-date=9 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709094549/https://www.efl.com/news/2016/october/team-of-the-round-a-stand-out-xi-from-efl-cup-round-four/ |archive-date=9 July 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Alexander-Arnold's breakthrough into the first team was rewarded with a new long-term contract in November and he started in Liverpool's next EFL Cup match later that month against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. He was named [[man of the match]] for his performance after registering his first [[Assist (association football)|assist]] for the club by setting up [[Forward (association football)|striker]] [[Divock Origi]] for the opening goal of a 2–0 win for Liverpool.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/242420-trio-commit-long-term-futures-to-lfc-by-signing-new-deals ====2017–18: First Champions League final====
In the buildup to the [[2017–18 Liverpool F.C. season|2017–18 season]], regular right-back Clyne suffered a serious back injury which afforded Alexander-Arnold the opportunity to rotate with [[Joe Gomez (footballer)|Joe Gomez]] during the early stages of the campaign.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/292305-trent-alexander-arnold-nathaniel-clyne |title=Trent: Competition has to be a part of LFC – fighting for your place is healthy |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Lynch |first=David |date=28 February 2018 |access-date=6 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906200442/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/292305-trent-alexander-arnold-nathaniel-clyne |archive-date=6 September 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 15 August 2017, he scored his first goal for the club when he struck home from a [[Free kick (association football)|free kick]] in a 2–1 first leg [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] play-off round win over [[Bundesliga]] team [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|TSG Hoffenheim]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40924300 |title=1899 Hoffenheim 1–2 Liverpool |first=Phil |last=Dawkes |website=BBC Sport |date=15 August 2017 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311004806/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40924300 |archive-date=11 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> In doing so, he became the third youngest player to score on his European debut for Liverpool, after [[Michael Owen]] and [[David Fairclough]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lfchistory.net/Stats/DebutGoalAges |title=Youngest debut goalscorers |website=LFCHistory.net |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816105236/http://www.lfchistory.net/Stats/DebutGoalAges |archive-date=16 August 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> During the group stages of the competition, Alexander-Arnold scored again in a 7–0 [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] win over [[NK Maribor|Maribor]] on 17 October, a result which was the joint-largest ever away win in the competition, and largest away win by an English club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-za/news/liverpool-record-champions-league-firsts-with-seven-goal-mauling-/1lddar82iw4ma19djblaj0b0fg |title=Liverpool record Champions League firsts with seven goal Mauling |first=Chris |last=Burton |website=Goal |publisher=Perform Group |date=17 October 2017 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311005305/http://www.goal.com/en-za/news/liverpool-record-champions-league-firsts-with-seven-goal-mauling-/1lddar82iw4ma19djblaj0b0fg |archive-date=11 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> He then scored his first Premier League goal for Liverpool on 26 December in a 5–0 home win over [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/12/26/liverpool-vs-swansea-city-premier-league-live-score-updates/ |title=Liverpool 5 Swansea City 0: Roberto Firmino stars in five-goal rout of Swans |first1=Chris |last1=Bascombe |first2=JJ |last2=Bull |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=26 December 2017 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311005516/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/12/26/liverpool-vs-swansea-city-premier-league-live-score-updates/ |archive-date=11 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Trent Alexander-Arnold 2017-09-26 1.jpg|thumb|upright|Alexander-Arnold lining up for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2017]]

In March the following year, Alexander-Arnold endured his most difficult spell with the club to date, after struggling against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] winger [[Wilfried Zaha]] and Manchester United's [[Marcus Rashford]] in successive weeks.<ref name=JPA/> Nonetheless, he retained his position in Liverpool's starting line-up to become the youngest English player to start in a Champions League quarter-final match and performed strongly in a 3–0 win over English rivals [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in April. His performance saw him named man of the match and earned him praise from the media for his ability to nullify City winger [[Leroy Sané]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/liverpool-trent-alexanderarnold-champions-league-manchester-city-a8287331.html |title=Why Trent Alexander-Arnold's Liverpudlian roots mean so much in the era of football's global village |last=Liew |first=Jonathan |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=3 April 2018 |access-date=5 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180405181616/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/liverpool-trent-alexanderarnold-champions-league-manchester-city-a8287331.html |archive-date=5 April 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2018/04/liverpool-3-0-man-city-player-ratings-2/ |title=Liverpool 3–0 Man City: Player Ratings |date=4 April 2018 |website=This Is Anfield |publisher=Soccer Publishing |access-date=5 April 2018 |last=Twelves |first=Ben |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609141056/https://www.thisisanfield.com/2018/04/liverpool-3-0-man-city-player-ratings-2/ |archive-date=9 June 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He impressed again in the reverse fixture as Liverpool eliminated City 5–1 on [[Aggregate score|aggregate]] to advance to the semi-finals of the competition for the first time in 10 years.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/299076-trent-alexander-arnold-champions-league-as-roma |title='It means everything' – Trent on semi-final buzz |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Lynch |first=David |date=25 April 2018 |access-date=26 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180426150415/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/299076-trent-alexander-arnold-champions-league-as-roma |archive-date=26 April 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 10 May 2018, his domestic and European form was rewarded when he won the Liverpool Young Player of the Season award for the second season running.<ref name=YPOTY2>{{cite news |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/mohamed-salah-scoops-two-prizes-12514793 |title=Mohamed Salah scoops TWO prizes at Liverpool Players' Awards – before making frantic dash to London for FWA dinner |newspaper=Daily Mirror |location=London |last=Prenderville |first=Liam |date=10 May 2018 |access-date=10 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180529204746/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/mohamed-salah-scoops-two-prizes-12514793 |archive-date=29 May 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Later that month, he became the youngest Liverpool player to start in a [[2018 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]] when he was named in the starting line-up against two-time reigning champions, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. Tasked with marking [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], he performed admirably though Liverpool ultimately succumbed to a 3–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.90min.in/posts/6071918-champions-league-final-player-ratings-from-real-madrid-s-3-1-win-over-liverpool |title=Champions League Final: Player Ratings From Real Madrid's 3–1 Win Over Liverpool |website=90min |publisher=HT Media |last=Chakraborty |first=Sushan |date=26 May 2018 |access-date=26 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190617135301/http://www.90min.in/posts/6071918-champions-league-final-player-ratings-from-real-madrid-s-3-1-win-over-liverpool |archive-date=17 June 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/may/26/real-madrid-liverpool-champions-league-final-match-report |title=Real Madrid win Champions League as brilliant Bale sinks Liverpool |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |date=26 May 2018 |access-date=27 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527054707/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/may/26/real-madrid-liverpool-champions-league-final-match-report |archive-date=27 May 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Following the conclusion of the season, in which he scored three goals in 33 appearances across all competitions, he was nominated for the [[Golden Boy (award)|Golden Boy]] award where he was later voted runner-up to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] defender, [[Matthijs de Ligt]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/305647-trent-alexander-arnold-ben-woodburn-herbie-kane-golden-boy-award |title=Liverpool trio nominated for 2018 Golden Boy award |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Williams |first=Sam |date=1 July 2018 |access-date=2 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180701194358/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/305647-trent-alexander-arnold-ben-woodburn-herbie-kane-golden-boy-award |archive-date=1 July 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.tuttosport.com/news/calcio/golden-boy/2018/12/17-51186728/golden_boy_2018_il_trionfo_di_de_ligt/?a=2 |title=Golden Boy 2018, il trionfo di De |url-status=live}}</ref>

====2018–19: Regular starter and Champions League title====
During the early stages of the [[2018–19 Premier League|following season]], he made his 50th appearance for Liverpool when he started in a 2–1 victory over Tottenham; the same opposition against whom he had made his debut almost two years prior.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/316433-tottenham-liverpool-talking-points-firmino-wijnaldum |title=Spurs 1–2 Liverpool: |url-status=live}}</ref> In October, he was one of 10 players nominated for the inaugural [[Kopa Trophy]], an award presented by ''[[France Football]]'' to the best young player under the age of 21, and ultimately ended sixth in the voting polls, having received votes from Owen, [[Denis Law]] and [[Pavel Nedvěd]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/320342-alexander-arnold-kopa-trophy-shortlist |title=Trent named on Kopa Trophy shortlist |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Shaw |first=Chris |date=8 |archive-date=17 June 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/6239498-the-4-former-ballon-d-or-winners-who-voted-for-trent-alexander-arnold-in-kopa-trophy 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He continued to enhance his burgeoning reputation in the months thereafter and was consistently listed in reports by the [[International Centre for Sports Studies|CIES]] as the world's most valuable [[Full-back (association football)|full-back]] from a transfer value perspective.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.football-observatory.com/IMG/sites/b5wp/2018/239/en/ |title=Updated transfer valuations: Mbappé takes the lead |publisher=International Centre for Sports Studies (CIES) |first1=Raffaele |last1=Poli |first2=Roger |last2=Besson |first3=Loïc |last3=Ravenel |date=5 November 2018 |access-date=5 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181218074805/http://www.football-observatory.com/IMG/sites/b5wp/2018/239/en/ |archive-date=18 December 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.football-observatory.com/IMG/sites/b5wp/2018/245/en/ |title=Brand new list of top transfer values for big-5 league players |publisher=International Centre for Sports Studies (CIES) |first1=Raffaele |last1=Poli |first2=Roger |last2=Besson |first3=Loïc |last3=Ravenel |date=7 January 2019 |access-date=10 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110033505/http://www.football-observatory.com/IMG/sites/b5wp/2018/245/en/ |archive-date=10 January 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> Alexander-Arnold elevated his game further following the turn of the year and, on 27 February 2019, became the youngest player, aged 20 years and 143 days, to record three assists in a single Premier League match when he set up [[Sadio Mané]] twice and [[Virgil van Dijk]] once in a 5–0 win over [[Watford F.C.|Watford]].<ref name=eply>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-bh/news/alexander-arnold-sets-premier-league-assist-record-as/4wshhjhdp0591h1napipkpbqf |title=Alexander-Arnold sets Premier League assist record as Liverpool crush |url-status=live}}</ref> Less than two months later, he became the fifth-youngest player to reach 50 Premier League appearances for the club, behind Owen, [[Raheem Sterling]], [[Robbie Fowler]] and Gerrard, when he started in a 3–1 win over [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/344571-alexander-arnold-50-premier-league-appearances [[File:LFC Parade 2019 01 (TAA).jpg|thumb|upright|Alexander-Arnold during [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s victory parade after winning the [[2019 UEFA Champions League final]]]]

Alexander-Arnold's creative prowess came to the fore once again in May when, during a 3–2 win over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], Alexander-Arnold equalled the Premier League record for the most assists by a defender in a season, with his two assists in the match raising his tally to 11. It also saw him and Robertson, who had 11 assists of his own, become the first set of defenders from the same team to record double figures for assists in the same season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/liverpools-flying-full-backs-alexander-arnold-and-robertson-make-/51evp7ilin7u1iwpzo39njjm3 |title=Liverpool's flying full-backs Alexander-Arnold and Robertson make Premier League assist history |website=Goal |publisher=Perform Group |date=4 May 2019 |access-date=5 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190506000420/https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/liverpools-flying-full-backs-alexander-arnold-and-robertson-make-/51evp7ilin7u1iwpzo39njjm3 |archive-date=6 May 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, with Liverpool trailing [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] 3–0 on aggregate after a first-leg defeat, he recorded two more assists, including an "instinctive corner" for Origi's winning goal, to help the club to a 4–3 aggregate victory and progress to a second consecutive Champions League final.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/liverpool/liverpool-fc-vs-fc-barcelona-trent-alexander-arnold-explains-match-winning-assist-a4136491.html |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold explains match-winning assist for Liverpool vs Barcelona |newspaper=Evening Standard |last=Ouzia |first=Malik |date=7 May 2019 |access-date=7 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507223549/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/liverpool/liverpool-fc-vs-fc-barcelona-trent-alexander-arnold-explains-match-winning-assist-a4136491.html |archive-date=7 May 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> On the final day of the domestic season, Alexander-Arnold assisted Mané in a 2–0 win over [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] to break the Premier League record for the most assists by a defender in a domestic campaign, with 12, surpassing previous holders [[Andy Hinchcliffe]], [[Leighton Baines]] and Robertson.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-sa/news/alexander-arnold-breaks-premier-league-assist-record-for/19g1z8vb0ysak180ioqdnhukdn |title=Alexander-Arnold breaks Premier League assist record for defenders |website=Goal |publisher=Perform Group |date=12 May 2019 |access-date=13 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190513062608/https://www.goal.com/en-sa/news/alexander-arnold-breaks-premier-league-assist-record-for/19g1z8vb0ysak180ioqdnhukdn |archive-date=13 May 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.statsperform.com/resource/hes-running-the-game-from-right-back-sit-back-and-watch-a-trent-alexander-arnold-data-dive/ |title=He's Running The Game From Right-Back: Sit Back And Watch A Trent Alexander-Arnold Data Dive |website=StatsPerform |publisher=Opta |last=Hopkins |first=Oliver|access-date=17 April 2020|archive-date=25 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925035712/https://www.statsperform.com/resource/hes-running-the-game-from-right-back-sit-back-and-watch-a-trent-alexander-arnold-data-dive/|url-status=live}}</ref> He then started in the [[2019 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League Final]], a 2–0 win over Tottenham, and became the youngest player to start in two successive finals in the competition, breaking the record set by [[AC Milan]]'s [[Christian Panucci]] in 1995.<ref name=ucly>{{cite news |url=http://www.sportbible.com/football/news-liverpools-alexander-arnold-makes-champions-league-final-history-20190601 |title=Liverpool's Trent Alexander-Arnold Makes Champions League Final History |url-status=live}}</ref> He was later named in the competition's Team of the Season and nominated for the [[UEFA Club Football Awards#Best Defender|Defender of the Season]] award.<ref name=cltots>{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0252-0e99c3f9c0f4-c762bb0ec7f4-1000--uefa-champions-league-squad-of-the-season/ |title=UEFA Champions League Squad of the Season |publisher=UEFA |date=2 June 2019 |access-date=1 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712170609/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=2607890.html |archive-date=12 September 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====2019–20: Ballon d'Or nomination and Premier League title====
Alexander-Arnold began the [[2019–20 Liverpool F.C. season|2019–20 season]] with his position as Liverpool's right-back cemented, and provided the assist for Origi's goal in the club's 4–1 opening game win over [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]].<ref name="IrTimes1">{{cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/english-soccer/liverpool-hardly-break-sweat-to-leave-canaries-all-a-flutter-1.3982059 |title=Liverpool hardly break sweat to leave Canaries all a flutter |first=Andy |last=Hunter |newspaper=The Irish Times |date=9 August 2019 |access-date=31 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190810032544/https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/english-soccer/liverpool-hardly-break-sweat-to-leave-canaries-all-a-flutter-1.3982059 |archive-date=10 August 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> In doing so, he became only the eighth player in the Premier League era to register an assist in five consecutive games, and the first to do so for Liverpool.<ref name="Squawka">{{cite web |url=https://www.squawka.com/en/news/trent-alexander-arnold-matches-mesut-ozil-assist-liverpool |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold sets new Liverpool record by matching Mesut Özil feat |first=Chris |last=Smith |website=Squawka |date=9 August 2019 |access-date=31 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831222240/https://www.squawka.com/en/news/trent-alexander-arnold-matches-mesut-ozil-assist-liverpool |archive-date=31 August 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> He appeared in subsequent wins over Southampton and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], as well as in Liverpool's triumph over [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the [[2019 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] where he scored a penalty in the shoot-out.<ref name="Guardian1">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/aug/14/liverpool-chelsea-uefa-super-cup-match-report |title=Liverpool sink Chelsea to lift Super Cup thanks to Adrián shootout save |first=Daniel |last=Taylor |newspaper=The Guardian |date=14 August 2019 |access-date=31 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211054748/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/aug/14/liverpool-chelsea-uefa-super-cup-match-report |archive-date=11 December 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> He then scored his first goal of the season during Liverpool's 2–1 league win over the Blues from a set-piece routine that was later nominated for the [[Premier League Goal of the Month]] award.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1366583 |title=Who of Willems, Tomori, Djenepo, Hendrick, Maddison, Cresswell, Alexander-Arnold or Kante produced the finest effort? |publisher=Premier League |date=4 October 2019|access-date=4 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007074305/https://www.premierleague.com/news/1366583|archive-date=7 October 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> The following month, he was nominated for the [[2019 Ballon d'Or]] award, alongside six of his Liverpool teammates.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/365217-salah-alexander-arnold-mane-alisson-wijnaldum-firmino-van-dijk-ballon-dor-shortlist |title=Seven Liverpool stars named on Ballon d'Or shortlist |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Shaw |first=Chris |date=21 October 2019|access-date=22 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022081916/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/365217-salah-alexander-arnold-mane-alisson-wijnaldum-firmino-van-dijk-ballon-dor-shortlist|archive-date=22 October 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 2 November, at the age of 21 years and 26 days, he became the fourth-youngest player to reach 100 appearances for Liverpool, behind Owen, Sterling and Fowler, and marked the occasion by assisting Mané for the winning goal in a 2–1 victory over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/370994-trent-alexander-arnold-100-games-landmark |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold becomes fourth-quickest to LFC landmark |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Carroll |first=James |date=2 November 2019|access-date=2 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191102173353/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/370994-trent-alexander-arnold-100-games-landmark|archive-date=2 November 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Exactly one month later, he was voted as the 19th-best player in the world at the Ballon d'Or ceremony, and the highest-ranked full-back.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/376000-virgil-van-dijk-ballon-dor-result |title=Virgil van Dijk finishes runner-up for 2019 Ballon d'Or |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=2 December 2019|access-date=3 December 2019 |last=Shaw |first=Chris|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203022116/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/376000-virgil-van-dijk-ballon-dor-result|archive-date=3 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpool.com/liverpool-fc-news/features/ballon-dor-liverpool-award-list-17353826 |title=The Liverpool achievement nobody noticed simply adds to what everybody already knew |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Morgan |first=Dan |date=3 December 2019|access-date=3 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203100410/https://www.liverpool.com/liverpool-fc-news/features/ballon-dor-liverpool-award-list-17353826|archive-date=3 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> He then made his [[FIFA Club World Cup]] debut during Liverpool's 2–1 semi-final win over reigning [[CONCACAF Champions League|CONCACAF]] champions [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]], and provided the match-winning assist for [[Roberto Firmino]] in stoppage time after coming on as a substitute for [[James Milner]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/12/18/football/1576698480_639915.html |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold tops 2019 Premier League assists chart |newspaper=Diario AS |location=Madrid |last=Roche |first=Calum |date=18 December 2019|access-date=19 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191219072505/https://en.as.com/en/2019/12/18/football/1576698480_639915.html|archive-date=19 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, he started and played the full 120 minutes as Liverpool were crowned champions for the first time in the club's history following a 1–0 win after [[Extra time (association football)|extra time]] over [[Copa Libertadores]] champions [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50869633 |title=Flamengo 0–1: Roberto Firmino's extra-time strike delivers first Club World Cup for Liverpool |website=BBC Sport |date=21 December 2019|access-date=22 December 2019 |last=Poole |first=Harry|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200103095346/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50869633|archive-date=3 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Upon returning from Qatar, Liverpool recorded a 4–0 league win over second-placed [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] during a match in which Alexander-Arnold played a hand in all four goals by scoring one, assisting two, and winning a penalty which was converted by Milner.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2019/dec/26/liverpool-right-back-playmaker-trent-alexander-arnold-leicester |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold is a unique playmaker in Liverpool's red machine |date=26 December 2019|access-date=4 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200102150023/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2019/dec/26/liverpool-right-back-playmaker-trent-alexander-arnold-leicester|archive-date=2 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> He was later rewarded for his form with the [[Premier League Player of the Month]] award, becoming the first full-back to claim the honour since [[Micah Richards]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1563909 |title=Alexander-Arnold wins EA SPORTS Player of the Month |publisher=Premier League |date=10 January 2020 |access-date=10 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110230646/https://www.premierleague.com/news/1563909 |archive-date=10 January 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> Further recognition followed at the turn of the year, when he was named in the [[UEFA Team of the Year#Team of the Year 2019|2019 UEFA Team of the Year]].<ref name=UTOTY>{{cite news |url=https://toty.uefa.com/reveal |title=Revealed – Team of the Year 2019 |date=15 January 2020|access-date=15 January 2020 |publisher=UEFA |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115123100/https://toty.uefa.com/reveal|archive-date=15 January 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> Alexander-Arnold then played a starring role in Liverpool's 2–1 win over Wolves as the club extended their unbeaten run in the league to 40 matches. During the encounter, he assisted captain [[Jordan Henderson]] for the opening goal and, in the process, became the first defender in the competition's history to reach double figures for assists in multiple campaigns.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2020/01/trent-delivers-a-premier-league-first-5-key-stats-from-wolves-1-2-liverpool/ |title=Trent delivers a Premier League first – 5 key stats from Wolves 1–2 Liverpool |website=This Is Anfield |last=Lusby |first=Jack |date=24 January 2019|access-date=24 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200124152227/https://www.thisisanfield.com/2020/01/trent-delivers-a-premier-league-first-5-key-stats-from-wolves-1-2-liverpool/|archive-date=24 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Towards the end of February, following a 3–2 win over [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], he matched his league assist record from the season before and took his overall tally in the Premier League to 25, becoming the third-youngest player in the competition's history to reach a quarter-century of assists behind [[Cesc Fàbregas]] and [[Wayne Rooney]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11669/11942620/trent-alexander-arnolds-assist-record-for-liverpool-analysed |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold's assist record for Liverpool analysed |website=Sky Sports |date=24 February 2020|access-date=25 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225064212/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11669/11942620/trent-alexander-arnolds-assist-record-for-liverpool-analysed|archive-date=25 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The season was temporarily suspended between March and June due to the outbreak of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], following which Alexander-Arnold helped Liverpool win their first league title in 30 years, and their first in the Premier League era.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2020/jun/25/liverpool-win-the-premier-league-title-live-reaction |title=Liverpool are crowned Premier League champions – reaction as it happened |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=26 June 2020|access-date=28 July 2020 |last1=McVeigh |last2=Smyth |last3=Hytner |last4=Graham |last5=Murray |first1=Niall |first2=Rob |first3=Mike |first4=Bryan |first5=Scott|archive-date=25 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925034725/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2020/jun/25/liverpool-win-the-premier-league-title-live-reaction/|url-status=live}}</ref> With the title secured, he then broke his own assist record on the penultimate day of the season when he set Firmino up to score in a 5–3 win over Chelsea.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.kickoff.com/news/articles/world-news/categories/news/english-premier-league/trent-alexander-arnold-breaks-premier-league-assist-record-again/682080 |title=Alexander-Arnold makes EPL history |last=Bekker |first=Liam |date=23 July 2020|access-date=28 July 2020|archive-date=25 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925034730/https://www.kickoff.com/news/articles/world-news/categories/news/english-premier-league/trent-alexander-arnold-breaks-premier-league-assist-record-again/682080/|url-status=live}}</ref> For his contributions during the season, he was awarded the inaugural [[Premier League Young Player of the Season]] award, won the PFA Young Player of the Year accolade and was named in the PFA Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Alexander-Arnold named TAG Heuer Young Player of the Season |publisher=Premier League |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1750635 |date=14 August name="auto1">{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/407814-five-reds-named-in-2019-20-pfa-team-of-the-year |title=Five Reds named in 2019–20 PFA Team of the Year |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Shaw |first=Chris |date=8 September 2020|access-date=8 September 2020|archive-date=25 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925034733/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/407814-five-reds-named-in-2019-20-pfa-team-of-the-year/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="auto3">{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/407827-trent-alexander-arnold-named-pfa-young-player-of-the-year |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold named PFA Young Player of the ====2020–21: Continued success====
Alexander-Arnold continued to feature prominently for Liverpool during the [[2020–21 Liverpool F.C. season|2020–21 season]] and, on 9 December, became the youngest player to captain the club in European competition, and third-youngest in any competition, when he donned the armband during a 1–1 Champions League draw against [[FC Midtjylland|Midtjylland]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/419354-trent-alexander-arnold-to-captain-liverpool-v-midtjylland |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold to captain Liverpool v Midtjylland |last=Shaw |first=Chris |date=9 December 2020|access-date=9 December 2020 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |archive-date=9 December that month, he was named in the 2020 [[FIFPro#FIFA FIFPRO Men's World 11|FIFA FIFPro Men's World 11]] alongside teammates [[Alisson Becker|Alisson]], Van Dijk and [[Thiago Alcântara|Thiago]], althewhile Liverpool set about its domestic title defence by topping the league standings by Christmas.<ref name=FIFPro>{{cite news |url=https://fifpro.org/en/industry/world-11/the-fifa-fifpro-men-s-world-11-of-2020 |title=The FIFA FIFPro Men's World 11 of 2019–2020 |publisher=FIFPro |date=17 December 2020|access-date=17 December 2020|archive-date=15 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210215035636/https://www.fifpro.org/en/industry/world-11/the-fifa-fifpro-men-s-world-11-of-2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://africa.espn.com/football/english-premier-league/story/4271594/why-liverpool-topping-the-premier-league-at-christmas-is-so-ominous-for-their-rivals-this-season |title=Why Liverpool topping
