====2021–22: Career milestones and domestic double====
[[File:Liverpool FC gegen 1. FSV Mainz 05 (Testspiel 23. Juli 2021) 23.jpg|thumb|upright|Alexander-Arnold playing for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2021]]

On 30 July, Alexander-Arnold signed a new long-term contract with Liverpool.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold signs new long-term contract with LFC |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/439450-trent-alexander-arnold-signs-new-long-term-contract-with-lfc |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=30 July 2021 |date=30 July 2021 |archive-date=30 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210730160637/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/439450-trent-alexander-arnold-signs-new-long-term-contract-with-lfc |url-status=live}}</ref> On 16 December, Alexander-Arnold scored Liverpool's third goal in a 3–1 home win against Newcastle United with a 25-yard strike into the top left corner of the goal in what was Liverpool's [[Football records and statistics in England#Wins|2,000th top-flight win]], the first club in English history to reach this landmark.<ref>{{cite news |title=Alexander-Arnold rocket seals win for Liverpool against spirited Newcastle |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/16/liverpool-newcastle-premier-league-match-report |access-date=16 December 2021 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |archive-date=5 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205094554/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/16/liverpool-newcastle-premier-league-match-report |url-status=live }}</ref> In May 2022, following Liverpool's victory over Chelsea in the [[2022 FA Cup Final]], Alexander-Arnold became the youngest-ever player to win six major trophies, namely the FIFA Club World Cup, UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup, Premier League, FA Cup and League Cup, for an English club, doing so at the age of 23 years and 219 days.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/may/15/alexander-arnold-hungry-for-more-liverpool-silverware-after-historic-feat |title=Alexander-Arnold hungry for more Liverpool silverware after historic feat |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |last=Hunter |first=Andy |date=15 May 2022 |accessdate=16 May 2022}}</ref> Alexander-Arnold came 22nd in the [[2022 Ballon d'Or]] as Liverpool narrowly missed out on a historic quadruple, finishing in 2nd place in the Premier League and once again losing the [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]] to Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Ballon d'Or Results |url=https://www.topendsports.com/sport/soccer/awards/ballondor-2022.htm |access-date=18 April 2023 |website=www.topendsports.com |archive-date=18 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418071627/https://www.topendsports.com/sport/soccer/awards/ballondor-2022.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Alexander-Arnold was selected as part of the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League#Team of the season|Champions League Team of the Season]].<ref name="auto5">{{cite news |title=2021/22 UEFA Champions League Team of the Season |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0275-154650014aef-02a394f30379-1000--official-team-of-the-season/ |publisher=UEFA |date=31 May 2022 |access-date=31 May 2022 |archive-date=6 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220606205239/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0275-154650014aef-02a394f30379-1000--official-team-of-the-season/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2022–23: Minor change of position and further success====
Following a sub-standard run of club form, Liverpool manager [[Jürgen Klopp]] decided to switch Alexander-Arnold to an inverted full-back role, allowing him to see more of the ball and play further up the pitch. In this role, Alexander-Arnold shifted next to a defensive midfielder, in front of three defenders, when Liverpool were in possession.<ref name="Athletic-evolve">{{cite news |last1=Pearce |first1=Andy Jones and James |title=How Trent Alexander-Arnold could evolve into Liverpool's midfield influencer |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4414520/2023/04/17/alexander-arnold-liverpool-midfield/ |website=The Athletic |date=17 April 2023 |access-date=5 September 2023 |language=en |archive-date=5 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905191950/https://theathletic.com/4414520/2023/04/17/alexander-arnold-liverpool-midfield/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This switch proved to be the catalyst for an improved run of individual and club form.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Match Report: Liverpool 1 Brentford 0|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65433560|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=6 May 2023|archive-date=5 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505155132/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65433560|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= Ibrahima Konate exclusive: Liverpool defender on Trent Alexander-Arnold, Champions League and new system |url=
https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11669/12871710/ibrahima-konate-exclusive-liverpool-defender-on-trent-alexander-arnold-champions-league-and-new-system |publisher=Sky Sports |access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= Jürgen Klopp on Trent Alexander-Arnold's central role for Liverpool and improved defending |url= https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12870834/jurgen-klopp-on-trent-alexander-arnolds-central-role-for-liverpool-and-improved-defending |publisher= Sky Sports |access-date= 6 May 2023 |archive-date= 6 May 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230506221258/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12870834/jurgen-klopp-on-trent-alexander-arnolds-central-role-for-liverpool-and-improved-defending |url-status= live }}</ref> On 17 April 2023, Alexander-Arnold provided his 50th assist in the Premier League in a victory away to Leeds United.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liverpool hit Leeds for six to boost European hopes |date=17 April 2023 |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/3158800 |publisher=Premier League |access-date=18 April 2023 |archive-date=18 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418085559/https://www.premierleague.com/news/3158800 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 30 April 2023, Alexander-Arnold became the first person to assist a goal in five consecutive Premier League matches twice.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold set an all-time Premier League record in Liverpool's meeting with Spurs |url=https://www.101greatgoals.com/news/trent-alexander-arnold-set-an-all-time-premier-league-record-in-liverpools-meeting-with-spurs/ |access-date=30 April 2023 |website=101 Great Goals |language=en |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603134056/https://www.101greatgoals.com/news/trent-alexander-arnold-set-an-all-time-premier-league-record-in-liverpools-meeting-with-spurs/ |url-status=live }}</ref> However, at the end of the [[2022–23 Liverpool F.C. season|2022–23 season]], Liverpool narrowly missed out on UEFA Champions League qualification.<ref>{{Cite news |title= Mohamed Salah 'totally devastated' Liverpool miss out on Champions League football: 'absolutely no excuse' |publisher= EuroSport |url= https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/premier-league/2022-2023/mohamed-salah-totally-devastated-liverpool-miss-out-on-champions-league-football-absolutely-no-excus_sto9623012/story.shtml |access-date= 29 May 2023 |archive-date= 13 July 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230713002337/https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/premier-league/2022-2023/mohamed-salah-totally-devastated-liverpool-miss-out-on-champions-league-football-absolutely-no-excus_sto9623012/story.shtml |url-status= live }}</ref>

====2023–24: vice-captaincy====
On 31 July 2023, following the departure of [[James Milner]], Alexander-Arnold was named as Liverpool's new vice-captain, acting as deputy to Virgil van Dijk.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carroll |first1=James |title=Virgil van Dijk named new Liverpool captain, Trent Alexander-Arnold vice-captain |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/virgil-van-dijk-named-new-liverpool-captain-trent-alexander-arnold-vice-captain |website=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=31 July 2023 |date=31 July 2023 |archive-date=31 July 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230731172715/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/virgil-van-dijk-named-new-liverpool-captain-trent-alexander-arnold-vice-captain |url-status=live }}</ref> On 25 November 2023, he scored his first goal of the [[2023–24 Liverpool F.C. season|2023–24 season]], an equaliser against Manchester City in a 1–1 draw at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Glendenning |first=Barry |date=25 November 2023 |title=Manchester City 1–1 Liverpool: Premier League – as it happened |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2023/nov/25/manchester-city-v-liverpool-premier-league-live |access-date=25 November 2023 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> On 7 January 2024, during a match against Arsenal, Alexander-Arnold hyperextended his knee, causing him to suffer a small tear in a lateral ligament. He was ruled out for an estimated three weeks following the injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 January 2024 |title=Liverpool defender Trent Alexander-Arnold to miss three weeks because of a knee injury |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/soccer/liverpool-defender-trent-alexander-arnold-to-miss-three-weeks-because-of-a-knee-injury/article_fcefcc1a-07ea-51b8-b8bd-d904bfeeb914.html |access-date=9 January 2024 |publisher=Toronto Star |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=10 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240110012714/https://www.thestar.com/sports/soccer/liverpool-defender-trent-alexander-arnold-to-miss-three-weeks-because-of-a-knee-injury/article_fcefcc1a-07ea-51b8-b8bd-d904bfeeb914.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 10 February, he assisted Diogo Jota's goal against Burnley, making him the defender with the highest number of assists in Premier League history, overtaking his Liverpool teammate Andy Robertson.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander-Arnold sets record for defenders' Premier League assists |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/3889135 |access-date=11 February 2024 |website=www.premierleague.com |date=10 February 2024 |archive-date=11 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240211130000/https://www.premierleague.com/news/3889135 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2024–25: Second Premier League title and departure====
On 17 August 2024, Alexander-Arnold started at right back and played 76 minutes in [[Arne Slot]]'s first match as Liverpool manager, a 2–0 win over [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] in the team's opening match of the [[2024–25 Premier League|2024–25 Premier League season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cn02gdl9wyvo|title='Breathtaking football' – how Slot's Liverpool machine kicked into gear|date=17 August 2024|access-date=21 April 2025|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=14 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114152910/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cn02gdl9wyvo|url-status=live}}</ref> During the 3–3 draw against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[St. James' Park]], Alexander-Arnold contributed two assists from the substitutes bench, becoming the first defender in Premier League history to record 60 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Henry |date=5 December 2024 |title=Trent sets new Premier League assist record after superb cameo |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2024/12/trent-alexander-arnold-sets-new-premier-league-assist-record-after-superb-cameo/ |access-date=6 December 2024 |website=This Is Anfield |archive-date=5 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241205102810/https://www.thisisanfield.com/2024/12/trent-alexander-arnold-sets-new-premier-league-assist-record-after-superb-cameo/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 29 December, he scored his first goal of the season in a 5–0 away win at [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in the Premier League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/west-ham-united-vs-liverpool/report/505996|title=West Ham 0–5 Liverpool: Mohamed Salah stars as Reds maintain Premier League title charge|date=29 December 2024|access-date=21 April 2025|website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

On 11 January 2025, Alexander-Arnold captained the Liverpool team and scored the second goal in the club's 4–0 win over [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] in the third round of the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cd9x10239p2t|title=Liverpool 4–0 Accrington Stanley: Federico Chiesa scores first Reds goal in third-round win|date=11 January 2025|access-date=21 April 2025|website=BBC}}</ref> On 11 March, Alexander-Arnold was substituted with an ankle injury in Liverpool's 1–0 defeat to [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|round of 16]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/liverpool-psg-champions-league-result-report-b2713239.html|title=Liverpool are out of the Champions League but the worst could be yet to come|date=12 March 2025|website=The Independent|access-date=21 April 2025|archive-date=17 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317151003/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/liverpool-psg-champions-league-result-report-b2713239.html|url-status=live}}</ref> This injury caused him to miss the next four matches including the [[2025 EFL Cup final]], which the club lost 2–1 to Newcastle United.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/efl-cup-final-newcastle-end-56-year-trophy-drought-top-liverpool-with-dominant-performance/live/|title=EFL Cup final: Newcastle end 56-year trophy drought, top Liverpool with dominant performance|date=16 March 2025|access-date=21 April 2025|website=CBS|archive-date=19 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250319064817/https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/efl-cup-final-newcastle-end-56-year-trophy-drought-top-liverpool-with-dominant-performance/live/|url-status=live}}</ref> He returned to the Liverpool squad on 20 April 2025, as a 71st-minute substitute against Leicester City, making his 350th appearance for the club. Five minutes later he scored the only goal of the match to take Liverpool within one win of securing a [[List of English football champions|20th English league title]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c93gwe70z4go|title='Iconic moment in a special Liverpool career – but was it a farewell?'|date=20 April 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 5 May 2025, eight days after winning the Premier League title, Alexander-Arnold announced that he had decided to leave Liverpool at the end of the season, bringing an end to his 20 year association with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 May 2025 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold to leave LFC at end of contract |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/trent-alexander-arnold-leave-lfc-end-contract |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250505123036/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/trent-alexander-arnold-leave-lfc-end-contract |archive-date=5 May 2025 |access-date=5 May 2025 |website= |publisher=Liverpool FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>
===Real Madrid===
On 30 May 2025, [[La Liga]] club Real Madrid announced the signing of Alexander-Arnold on a six-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 May 2025 |title=Official Announcement: Alexander-Arnold |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-30-05-2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530102550/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-30-05-2025 |archive-date=30 May 2025 |access-date=30 May 2025 |publisher=[[Real Madrid CF]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=30 May 2025 |title=Alexander-Arnold signs for Real Madrid |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/perfil-arnold-30-05-2025 |access-date=30 May 2025 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> Despite being considered as a free agent if the transfer confirmation happened in July, Real Madrid paid Liverpool a fee in order to secure the transfer before Alexander-Arnold's contract expired on 30 June,<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 May 2025 |title=Liverpool accept Real Madrid offer for Trent Alexander-Arnold transfer |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-accept-real-madrid-offer-trent-alexander-arnold-transfer |access-date=31 May 2025 |publisher=Liverpool FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> so that he would be able to represent the club in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]], with [[BBC Sport|the BBC]], [[The Athletic]] and Spanish sources reporting the fee to be between €6.2m and €10m.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mokbel |first=Sami |date=30 May 2025 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold transfer: Real Madrid pay Liverpool for early signing |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cz01k8nje54o |access-date=30 May 2025 |publisher=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |user=Ramon_AlvarezMM |number= 1928449615029776761 |title= Según mi información el Real Madrid paga al Liverpool 5,3 millones de libras. Es decir, unos 6,2 millones de euros. Por supuesto respeto la información que se ha dado desde otros medios. |date=May 30, 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Ornstein |first1=David |last2=Cortegana |first2=Mario |date=30 May 2025 |title=Real Madrid to pay Liverpool €10m for Trent Alexander-Arnold to join for Club World Cup |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6334302/2025/05/30/trent-alexander-arnold-real-madrid-transfers-liverpool-club-world-cup/ |access-date=31 May 2025 |publisher=The Athletic |language=en-GB}}</ref> He became the seventh Englishman to join ''Los Blancos'' in the professional era.<ref name="7th English">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jun/14/from-beckham-to-bale-british-players-real-madrid-jude-bellingham |title=From Beckham to Bale: the history of British players at Real Madrid |website=Guardian Sport |date=14 June 2023 |access-date=31 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231013202902/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jun/14/from-beckham-to-bale-british-players-real-madrid-jude-bellingham |archive-date=13 October 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>{{efn-ua|The previous six were [[Laurie Cunningham]], [[Steve McManaman]], [[David Beckham]], [[Michael Owen]], [[Jonathan Woodgate]] and [[Jude Bellingham]].<ref name="7th English" />}} On 11 June, he was officially unveiled as a new player for Real Madrid at a ceremony held at Real Madrid City.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-11 |title=Alexander-Arnold unveiled as new Real Madrid player |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/alexander-arnold-presentado-como-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-12-06-2025 |access-date=2025-06-12 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> Real Madrid president [[Florentino Pérez]] welcomed Alexander-Arnold, presenting him with the club's iconic white shirt bearing the number 12, a departure from the number 66 he previously wore during his time at Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-11 |title=Alexander-Arnold signs contract with Real Madrid |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/alexander-arnold-firmo-su-contrato-con-el-real-madrid-12-06-2025 |access-date=2025-06-12 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> He also switched the name on the back of his shirt from ‘Alexander-Arnold’ to ‘Trent’ in order to avoid confusion for Spanish fans.<ref name=":0" />

On 18 June 2025, Alexander-Arnold made his debut for Real Madrid in a [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup Group H|group stage]] match against [[Al-Hilal Saudi FC|Al-Hilal]] at the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]], which resulted in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 Jun 2025 |title=Bounou saves spot-kick as Hilal hold Real |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/club-world-cup/usa-2025/articles/real-madrid-al-hilal-highlights-match-report |access-date=18 Jun 2025 |publisher=[[FIFA]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ronay |first=Barney |date=2025-06-18 |title=Alexander-Arnold feels heat on Real Madrid debut as Al-Hilal make Club World Cup point |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jun/18/real-madrid-al-hilal-club-world-cup-match-report |access-date=2025-06-18 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He made his [[La Liga]] debut for Madrid on 19 August, in a 1–0 victory over [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 August 2025 |title=Real Madrid 1–0 Osasuna: Mbappe penalty gives Alonso unconvincing win|url=https://www.fotmob.com/de/news/1i5wg7hruqaid1u0kv2calu9j5-real-madrid-1-0-osasuna-mbappe-penalty-gives-alonso-unconvincing-win|access-date=19 August 2025 |publisher=fotmob.com}}</ref>

On 4 November 2025, Alexander-Arnold returned to [[Anfield]] to play the final nine minutes of a [[2025-26 UEFA Champions League league phase|UEFA Champions League]] league phase match between Liverpool and Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McNulty |first=Phil |title=Liverpool 1-0 Real Madrid: Alexis Mac Allister scores with Reds back to their best to beat Real |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cg7nd3gpj8yt |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He received a hostile reception from the home crowd, and was constantly booed, notably when being substituted onto the pitch and when in possession of the ball.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-04 |title=Trent suffers boos and defeat on Liverpool return |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/46850595/trent-alexander-arnold-boos-liverpool-real-madrid |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> A mural of Alexander-Arnold unveiled in 2019 with his quote, ‘I am just a normal lad from Liverpool whose dream has just come true’ was also vandalised, with the word ‘rat’ being repeatedly sprayed onto the image.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pearce |first=James |date=November 5, 2025 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold mural in Liverpool vandalised ahead of return with Real Madrid |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6776395/2025/11/04/alexander-arnold-mural-liverpool-madrid/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The incident prompted widespread discussion among fans and pundits.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pearce |first=James |last2=Hughes |first2=Simon |last3=On |first3=Walk |date=2025-05-13 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold and Liverpool fans: A sensible conversation about booing |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6349659/2025/05/13/trent-alexander-arnold-booing-liverpool-fans-discussion/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Alexander-Arnold has represented England at various youth levels and featured at the [[2015 FIFA U-17 World Cup]] in Chile.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2018/jul/06/trent-alexander-arnold-grassroots-hero-060718 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold says his grasroots days in Liverpool don't feel that long ago |publisher=The Football Association |date=6 July 2018 |access-date=6 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180706184607/http://www.thefa.com/news/2018/jul/06/trent-alexander-arnold-grassroots-hero-060718 |archive-date=6 July 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> He also scored three goals for the [[England national under-19 football team|England U19]] team, including a brace against [[Croatia national under-19 football team|Croatia]] and another against [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain]] which secured England's qualification for the [[2017 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2016/nov/12/england-u19s-wales-report-121116 |title=A brace from Liverpool's Trent Alexander-Arnold not enough to rescue a draw in Bangor |publisher=The Football Association |date=12 November 2016 |access-date=29 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161115220418/http://www.thefa.com/news/2016/nov/12/england-u19s-wales-report-121116 |archive-date=15 November 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2017/mar/24/uefa-european-u19s-championship-elite-qualifying-round-england-3-0-spain-240317 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold at the Double as U19s qualify for Euros |publisher=The Football Association |date=24 March 2017 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170626004634/http://www.thefa.com/news/2017/mar/24/uefa-european-u19s-championship-elite-qualifying-round-england-3-0-spain-240317 |archive-date=26 June 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> He did not feature at the tournament itself as Liverpool reached an agreement with England to rest him ahead of the following season's league campaign, but the Three Lions went on to defeat [[Portugal national under-19 football team|Portugal]] in the final to claim their first ever title in the competition.<ref name=AK/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/jul/15/football-under-19-uefa-england-portugal-final |title=England win European Under-19 Championship as youth shines again |first=Nick |last=Ames |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=15 July 2017 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311010101/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/jul/15/football-under-19-uefa-england-portugal-final |archive-date=11 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The month following the tournament, he was called up to the [[England national under-21 football team|England U21]] team for the first time for their [[2019 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification|UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualifiers]] against [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands]] and [[Latvia national under-21 football team|Latvia]], and made his debut in a 3–0 win over the latter. Two more appearances followed with the U21 side before he was promoted and solidified his status within the senior [[England national football team|England]] camp.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2017/08/trent-alexander-arnold-earns-1st-england-u21s-call-among-3-liverpool-players/ |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold earns 1st England U21s call-up among 3 Liverpool players |first=Jack |last=Lusby |website=This Is Anfield |publisher=Soccer Publishing |date=24 August 2017 |access-date=11 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311010434/https://www.thisisanfield.com/2017/08/trent-alexander-arnold-earns-1st-england-u21s-call-among-3-liverpool-players/ |archive-date=11 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/sep/05/england-under-21-latvia-european-championship-qualifier-match-report |title=England Under-21s serve up exhilarating fare in easy victory over Latvia |first=Ben |last=Fisher |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=5 September 2017 |access-date=3 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104102613/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/sep/05/england-under-21-latvia-european-championship-qualifier-match-report |archive-date=4 November 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Senior===
[[File:Trent Alexander-Arnold.jpg|thumb|upright|Alexander-Arnold with [[England national football team|England]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]

In March 2018, while part of the U21 team, Alexander-Arnold was invited to train with the senior national team for the first time ahead of their friendly matches against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/294961-trent-alexander-arnold-england |title=Trent trains with senior England squad |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |last=Shaw |first=Chris |date=20 March 2018 |access-date=20 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180320231036/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/294961-trent-alexander-arnold-england |archive-date=20 March 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> He received his first call-up in May 2018 when he was named in Gareth Southgate's squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44138600 |title=England World Cup squad: Trent Alexander-Arnold in 23-man squad |website=BBC Sport |date=16 May 2018 |access-date=16 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180516133910/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44138600 |archive-date=16 May 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> His debut followed on 7 June 2018 when he started in a 2–0 pre-tournament friendly win over [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] at [[Elland Road]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44246164 |title=England 2–0 Costa Rica |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=7 June 2018 |access-date=7 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180607172849/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44246164 |archive-date=7 June 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Prior to the match, he was handed his match jersey by [[Prince William, Duke of Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/06/07/prince-william-visits-england-squad-presents-trent-alexander/ |title=Prince William visits England squad and presents Trent Alexander-Arnold with his match shirt |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |last=Johnson |first=Jamie |date=7 June 2018 |access-date=8 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180608024257/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/06/07/prince-william-visits-england-squad-presents-trent-alexander/ |archive-date=8 June 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Alexander-Arnold then made his debut in the competition on 28 June, starting in a 1–0 group-stage defeat to [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]], after both sides had already confirmed their progression to the knockout stages. In doing so, he became only the fourth teenager to start a match for England at a World Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/liverpool-teenager-alexander-arnold-joins-exclusive-england/va0gudxbok61m29jjimvulap |title=Liverpool teenager Alexander-Arnold joins exclusive England World Cup club |website=Goal |publisher=Perform Group |date=28 June 2018 |access-date=28 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180628230024/http://www.goal.com/en/news/liverpool-teenager-alexander-arnold-joins-exclusive-england/va0gudxbok61m29jjimvulap |archive-date=28 June 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> It remained, however, his only appearance as [[Kieran Trippier]] was preferred at right-back and featured throughout as England were defeated by [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] in the semi-finals, and then again by Belgium in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Third place play-off|third place play-off]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2018/07/liverpool-trio-not-involved-as-england-lose-to-belgium-in-world-cup-third-place-playoff/ |title=Liverpool trio not involved as England lose to Belgium in World Cup third-place playoff |website=This Is Anfield |publisher=Soccer Publishing |last=Matchett |first=Karl |date=14 July 2018 |access-date=15 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714212539/https://www.thisisanfield.com/2018/07/liverpool-trio-not-involved-as-england-lose-to-belgium-in-world-cup-third-place-playoff/ |archive-date=14 July 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 15 November 2018, during a friendly international, held in honour of Wayne Rooney, Alexander-Arnold scored his first senior international goal as England recorded a 3–0 win over the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45174412 |title=England 3–0 USA |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=15 November 2018 |access-date=15 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181115225704/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45174412 |archive-date=15 November 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> In doing so, and at the age of 20 years and 39 days, he became the youngest Liverpool player since Michael Owen in 1999 to score for the national team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/alexander-arnold-becomes-youngest-liverpool-player-in-20/2obs5nhfh92k1j3v8jugs8hd3 |title=Alexander-Arnold becomes youngest Liverpool player in 20 years to score for England |website=Goal |publisher=Perform Group |date=15 November 2018 |access-date=19 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181119132947/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/alexander-arnold-becomes-youngest-liverpool-player-in-20/2obs5nhfh92k1j3v8jugs8hd3 |archive-date=19 November 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> In June 2019, he was part of the England squad which ended third at the inaugural [[UEFA Nations League]] and played the full match in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] win over [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] in the third-place play-off.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jun/09/england-v-switzerland-nations-league-third-place-play-off-live |title=England beat Switzerland on penalties to secure third place in Nations League third place play-off |newspaper=The Guardian |date=9 June 2019 |access-date=9 June 2019 |last=Smyth |first=Rob |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609155807/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jun/09/england-v-switzerland-nations-league-third-place-play-off-live |archive-date=9 June 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> Two years later, he was named in England's 26-man squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2020]] but was forced to withdraw eight days before the competition commenced after sustaining a thigh injury during a pre-tournament friendly against [[Austria national football team|Austria]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.englandfootball.com/Articles/2021/Jun/03/20210603-trent-alexander-arnold-withdrawn-from-england-squad |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold withdrawn from squad |last=Walker |first=Andy |publisher=The Football Association |date=3 June 2021|access-date=4 June 2021|archive-date=4 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210604035757/https://www.englandfootball.com/Articles/2021/Jun/03/20210603-trent-alexander-arnold-withdrawn-from-england-squad|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 10 November 2022, he was named in England's 26-man squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Maddison, Rashford and Wilson make England squad |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63585869 |access-date=10 November 2022 |archive-date=25 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221125124014/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63585869 |url-status=live }}</ref> where he made one appearance against [[Wales national football team|Wales]] in the group stage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/how-trent-alexander-arnold-is-fighting-back-in-bid-to-turn-form-around-8gf2tp7lb|title=How Trent Alexander-Arnold is fighting back in bid to turn form around|date=27 February 2023|access-date=21 November 2023|website=The Times|archive-date=21 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250421114351/https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/how-trent-alexander-arnold-is-fighting-back-in-bid-to-turn-form-around-8gf2tp7lb|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 16 June 2023, Alexander-Arnold scored a long-ranged goal in a 4–0 victory in the [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying|UEFA Euro 2024 qualifiers]] against [[Malta national football team|Malta]] and he was described by Jacob Steinberg of the Guardian as having "oozed class".<ref>{{Cite news |title= Alexander-Arnold shows again he is a talent England cannot afford to waste |website=The Guardian |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jun/16/alexander-arnold-shows-again-he-is-a-talent-england-cannot-afford-to-waste |access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title= Malta 0–4 England: Trent Alexander-Arnold impresses in advanced position for Three Lions |website= [[BBC Sport]] |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65936430 |access-date= 17 June 2023 |archive-date= 17 June 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230617063641/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65936430 |url-status= live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title= Trent Alexander-Arnold: England star 'feels natural' in new midfield role after Malta display |website= [[BBC Sport]] |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65935420 |access-date= 18 June 2023 |archive-date= 17 June 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230617212619/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65935420 |url-status= live }}</ref> Alexander-Arnold played in the same 'Number 10' role in the next game and was likewise praised.<ref>{{Cite news |title= England 7 North Macedonia 0 |website= [[BBC Sport]] |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65874634 |access-date= 19 June 2023 |archive-date= 19 June 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230619221620/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65874634 |url-status= live }}</ref>

On 3 June 2024, in a Euro 2024 warm-up match against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], Alexander-Arnold scored his third England goal and was named Player of the Match as the team won 3–0.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ck5544lk7j3t|title=Hungary 1–3 Switzerland LIVE: UEFA Euro 2024 – score, updates & reaction|website=BBC Sport|access-date=17 June 2024|archive-date=8 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008021116/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ck5544lk7j3t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, he was named in England's 26-man squad for [[UEFA Euro 2024]], where he was listed as a midfielder<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cv22menk7dno |title=Eze & Wharton named in England squad for Euro 2024 |website=BBC Sport |date=6 June 2024 |access-date=6 June 2024 |archive-date=6 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240606170808/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cv22menk7dno |url-status=live }}</ref> and assigned the number 8 shirt.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2024/Jun/08/england-euro-2024-squad-numbers-confirmed-2024806|title=England Euro 2024 squad numbers confirmed|date=8 June 2024|website=England Football|access-date=17 June 2024|archive-date=19 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619194108/https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2024/Jun/08/england-euro-2024-squad-numbers-confirmed-2024806|url-status=live}}</ref>

Alexander-Arnold started England's opening match of Euro 2024, partnering [[Declan Rice]] in central midfield as the team beat [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] 1–0 in Gelsenkirchen. He played 69 minutes before being substituted for [[Conor Gallagher]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cz992dxd4xwt#Line-ups|title=Hungary 1–3 Switzerland LIVE: UEFA Euro 2024 – score, updates & reaction|website=BBC Sport|access-date=17 June 2024|archive-date=17 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240617013156/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cz992dxd4xwt#Line-ups|url-status=live}}</ref> He went on to start the second match against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]], being substituted for Gallagher in the 54th minute,<ref name="UEFA">{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028e-1b2dd93b650a-1e25fab680c2-1000--denmark-1-1-england-hjulmand-stunner-cancels-out-kane-strike/|title=Denmark 1–1 England: Hjulmand stunner cancels out Kane strike|date=20 June 2024|access-date=25 June 2024|website=UEFA|archive-date=21 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240621151619/https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028e-1b2dd93b650a-1e25fab680c2-1000--denmark-1-1-england-hjulmand-stunner-cancels-out-kane-strike/|url-status=live}}</ref> before playing the final six minutes of the final match against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]] as a substitute for [[Kieran Trippier]].<ref name="UEFA"/> In the [[UEFA Euro 2024 knockout stage|quarter-final]] against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]], Alexander-Arnold appeared as a substitute for [[Phil Foden]] in the 25th minute of extra time and scored England's decisive fifth kick of the penalty shootout.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028f-1b4e143fd946-8d1c55ab8bed-1000--england-1-1-switzerland-aet-5-3-pens-pickford-and-saka-l/|title=England 1–1 Switzerland (5–3 pens): Pickford and Saka lead England to semi-finals|date=6 July 2024|website=[[UEFA]]|access-date=7 July 2024|archive-date=7 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240707045212/https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028f-1b4e143fd946-8d1c55ab8bed-1000--england-1-1-switzerland-aet-5-3-pens-pickford-and-saka-l/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Player profile==
===Style of play===
Alexander-Arnold is widely acknowledged for his range of passing, crossing and assists, although he has received some criticism from some pundits and fans for his defensive capabilities.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jamie Carragher: Trent Alexander-Arnold's defending not good enough, he needs competition at Liverpool |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12835255/jamie-carragher-trent-alexander-arnolds-defending-not-good-enough-he-needs-competition-at-liverpool |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230316121924/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12835255/jamie-carragher-trent-alexander-arnolds-defending-not-good-enough-he-needs-competition-at-liverpool |date=16 March 2023 |archive-date=16 March 2023 |website=Sky Sports |last=Carragher |first=Jamie |location=UK}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Is Trent Alexander-Arnold really the problem for Liverpool defensively? Here's why it's complicated |url=https://www.espn.com/sports/insider/soccer/insider/story/_/id/34742151/is-trent-alexander-arnold-liverpool-defensive-liability |archive-url=https://archive.today/20221007141927/https://www.espn.com/sports/insider/soccer/insider/story/_/id/34742151/is-trent-alexander-arnold-liverpool-defensive-liability |date=7 October 2022 |archive-date=7 October 2022 |last=O'Hanlon |first=Ryan |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title='Absolutely obscene' – Every word Gary Neville said in detailed analysis of Trent Alexander-Arnold at Liverpool |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/gary-neville-trent-alexander-arnold-25169749 |date=3 October 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230316122611/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/gary-neville-trent-alexander-arnold-25169749 |archive-date=16 March 2023 |last=Newbould |first=Kyle |newspaper=Liverpool Echo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Surely We Can Stop Talking About Trent Alexander-Arnold |url=https://liverpooloffside.sbnation.com/2022/11/7/23445171/media-obsession-trent-alexander-arnold-world-cup-qatar-opinion-liverpool-england |date=7 November 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230316122539/https://liverpooloffside.sbnation.com/2022/11/7/23445171/media-obsession-trent-alexander-arnold-world-cup-qatar-opinion-liverpool-england |archive-date=16 March 2023 |last=Lewis |first=Mari |work=SB Nation}}</ref>

During the early years of his career, he emerged as one of the Premier League's most creative players due to his role in assisting goals from early [[Cross (association football)|crosses]] and set-piece deliveries.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/how-liverpools-trent-alexander-arnold-17446072 |title=Liverpool's Trent Alexander-Arnold has surpassed Man City's Kevin De Bruyne to cement midfield calls |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |last=Dunn |first=Connor |date=20 December 2019|access-date=26 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191226084051/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/how-liverpools-trent-alexander-arnold-17446072|archive-date=26 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> He possesses an impressive passing range, which is attributed to his development as a [[midfielder]] during his time in Liverpool's youth academy, and has been one of Liverpool's designated set-piece specialists for deadball situations since the 2017–18 season.<ref name=sop1>{{cite news |url=http://africa.espn.com/soccer/blog/tactics-and-analysis/67/post/3710971/trent-alexander-arnold-is-already-a-world-class-full-back-but-he-might-not-be-there-for-long |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold is already a world-class full-back but he might not be there for long |publisher=ESPN |last=Cox |first=Michael |date=28 November 2018 |access-date=29 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229171808/http://africa.espn.com/soccer/blog/tactics-and-analysis/67/post/3710971/trent-alexander-arnold-is-already-a-world-class-full-back-but-he-might-not-be-there-for-long |archive-date=29 December 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=sop2>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45187181 |title=Liverpool: Why Trent Alexander-Arnold can back up the hype |website=BBC Sport |last=Sanders |first=Emma |date=22 August 2018 |access-date=29 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190102211032/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45187181 |archive-date=2 January 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> His set-piece routine, which involves three parallel steps backwards and one to the right, has been likened to that of former [[rugby union]] player [[Jonny Wilkinson]].<ref name=sop3>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/trent-alexander-arnold-my-dead-ball-routine-is-like-jonny-wilkinsons-6kqrjskzl |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold: 'My dead-ball routine is like Jonny Wilkinson's' |newspaper=The Times |date=21 December 2019|access-date=26 December 2019 |last=Robinson |first=Mark|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191225154301/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/trent-alexander-arnold-my-dead-ball-routine-is-like-jonny-wilkinsons-6kqrjskzl|archive-date=25 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Alexander-Arnold's craft and intelligence from deadball situations was singled out for particular praise by [[Gary Lineker]] and Cesc Fàbregas after he assisted the winning goal in the 2018–19 Champions League semi-final against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] by delivering a quickly-taken corner while the opposition players had their backs turned.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2019/05/08/gary-lineker-and-cesc-fabregas-react-to-trent-alexander-arnolds/ |title=Gary Lineker and Cesc Fabregas React to Trent Alexander-Arnold's Assist |website=[[HITC]] |publisher=GRV Media |date=8 May 2019|access-date=4 January 2020|archive-date=10 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110093507/https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2019/05/08/gary-lineker-and-cesc-fabregas-react-to-trent-alexander-arnolds/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Under Liverpool manager [[Jürgen Klopp]], whose tactical set-up placed creative responsibility on the shoulders of the club's full-backs, Alexander-Arnold was predominantly deployed down the right flank where his overlapping runs, switching of play, accuracy of crossing and work-rate in tracking back saw him become an important figure in the side's transitional style of play centred around high pressing.<ref name=sop3/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/18804/11374908/trent-alexander-arnold-on-the-rise-why-he-can-get-better-and-better |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold on the rise: Why he can get better and better |newspaper=Sky Sports |last=Bate |first=Adam |date=16 May 2018 |access-date=29 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229221737/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/18804/11374908/trent-alexander-arnold-on-the-rise-why-he-can-get-better-and-better |archive-date=29 December 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ccn.com/trent-alexander-arnold-is-reinventing-the-right-back-role-at-liverpool/ |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold Is Reinventing the Right-Back Role at Liverpool |website=CCN.com |publisher=Hawkfish AS |last=Lea |first=Greg |date=27 December 2019|access-date=28 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191228201822/https://www.ccn.com/trent-alexander-arnold-is-reinventing-the-right-back-role-at-liverpool/|archive-date=28 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Reception===
[[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] winner [[Cafu]] has praised Alexander-Arnold, saying "He's a sensational player, a rare talent. He's technically brilliant, he has so much quality. He has a Brazilian style of play. I love watching him play. And playing in such a great team will help him grow."<ref>{{cite web |title=Cafu: Ronaldinho was almost unmarkable |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/cafu-ronaldinho-was-almost-unmarkable-brazil-world-cup#cafu-and-david-beckham-lead-out-brazil-and-england-respectively-at-korea-japan-2 |publisher=FIFA |access-date=18 May 2021 |archive-date=18 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518162929/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/cafu-ronaldinho-was-almost-unmarkable-brazil-world-cup#cafu-and-david-beckham-lead-out-brazil-and-england-respectively-at-korea-japan-2 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Lionel Messi]] has called him "impressive" and remarked "[He is] the future, a fullback who is impressive going forward."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Owen |first1=Danny |title="Impressive" Lionel Messi raves about Liverpool youngster, says he's 'the future' |url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2020/04/01/do-impressive-lionel-messi-raves-about-liverpool-youngster-says/ |website=HITC |publisher=GRV Media |date=April 2020 |access-date=18 May 2021 |archive-date=18 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518162930/https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2020/04/01/do-impressive-lionel-messi-raves-about-liverpool-youngster-says/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Former Manchester United defender [[Gary Neville]] stated, "He's the best passer of a ball at right-back that I've ever seen. He's [[David Beckham]] and [[Kevin De Bruyne]] at right-back".<ref name="Passing">{{cite news |url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/09/14/soccer/1631631113_685262.html |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold is "like Beckham and de Bruyne, but at right-back" |newspaper=Diario AS |location=Madrid |date=14 September 2021|access-date = 8 October 2021|archive-date = 8 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211008224206/https://en.as.com/en/2021/09/14/soccer/1631631113_685262.amp.html|url-status = live}}</ref>

Alexander-Arnold has been the subject to criticism from some fans and pundits for his defensive capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moses |first=Martin |date=6 August 2022 |title=Fans tear into Trent Alexander-Arnold's defensive performance against Fulham |url=https://sportsbrief.com/football/liverpool/21422-fans-troll-trent-alexander-arnold-poor-defensive-skills-gift-aleksandar-mitrovic-opening-goal/ |access-date=8 August 2022 |website=SportsBrief |archive-date=4 April 2023 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Video Shows That Trent Alexander-Arnold Can't Defend And 'Proves His Haters Right' |url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/football-news-reactions-video-proves-that-liverpools-trent-alexander-arnold-cannot-defend-20210603 |access-date=8 August 2022 |website=sportbible.com |date=3 June 2021 |archive-date=4 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404040415/https://www.sportbible.com/football/football-news-reactions-video-proves-that-liverpools-trent-alexander-arnold-cannot-defend-20210603 James (footballer, born 1999)|Reece James]] and [[Kyle Walker]], with his defensive statistics ranking the best among them.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Danny |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold's defensive stats are the best among England's Euro 2020 right-backs |url=https://www.givemesport.com/1697177-trent-alexanderarnolds-defensive-stats-are-the-best-among-englands-euro-2020-rightbacks |website=Givemesport.com |date=26 May 2021 |publisher=Sports New Media |access-date=16 August 2022 |archive-date=16 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816205609/https://www.givemesport.com/1697177-trent-alexanderarnolds-defensive-stats-are-the-best-among-englands-euro-2020-rightbacks |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.premierleague.com/stats/player-comparison?player0Id=14571&player0isActive=1&player0compSeasonId=418&player1Id=14732&player1isActive=1&player1compSeasonId=418 |title= Player Comparison: Reece James against Trent Alexander-Arnold (see 2022–2023 season) |publisher= Premier League |access-date= 11 April 2023 |archive-date= 16 April 2023 |archive-url= |url-status= live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.thesportreview.com/article/trent-alexander-arnold-vs-reece-james/ |title= Trent Alexander-Arnold vs Reece James – What Do The Stats Say? |date= 29 August 2022 |publisher=The Sport Review |access-date=11 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61302842 |title= FA Cup final: Trent Alexander-Arnold versus Reece James in battle of the full-backs |work= BBC Sport |access-date= 11 April 2023 |archive-date= 19 April 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230419133614/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61302842 |url-status= live }}</ref> He has been defended by Klopp, who said "If anyone says Trent can't defend, they should come to me and I'll knock them down. I cannot hear that anymore, I don't know what the boy has to do!"<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bosher |first1=Luke |title='I'll knock them down' – Liverpool boss Klopp hits out at critics of Alexander-Arnold's defensive ability |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4181261/2022/03/17/ill-knock-them-down-liverpool-boss-klopp-hits-out-at-critics-of-alexander-arnolds-defensive-ability/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=16 August 2022 |archive-date=1 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221101153357/https://theathletic.com/news/ill-knock-them-down-liverpool-boss-klopp-hits-out-at-critics-of-alexander-arnolds-defensive-ability/hIz0mxiuhjFo/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Philanthropy==
Outside of football, Alexander-Arnold volunteers as an ambassador for the Liverpool-based charity ''An Hour for Others'', which seeks to provide underprivileged members of the community with anything from food hampers and toys to cooking and science lessons. He has supported the charity since being introduced to it by his mother in his mid-teens. During his time with Liverpool's academy, he and teammate Kris Owens pledged to support the initiative if either of them made it as professional footballers.<ref name=TG/> His philanthropy also expands beyond the charity and in March 2019, after signing a new boot sponsorship with [[Under Armour]] (the second most lucrative boot deal in England behind [[Harry Kane]]'s) he initiated plans to purchase plots in Liverpool and use the funds to construct new pitches for the community.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/trent-alexander-arnold-plans-pump-16008676 |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold plans to pump millions into Liverpool economy after signing lucrative Under Armour deal |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |last=Gors |first=Paul |date=21 March 2019 |access-date=21 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321164913/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/trent-alexander-arnold-plans-pump-16008676 |archive-date=21 March 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2020, Alexander-Arnold teamed up with Under Armour to support doctors, nurses, and key workers battling the COVID-19 Pandemic. Alexander-Arnold and Under Armour provided over 2,000 products for workers at the [[Royal Liverpool University Hospital]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dan |first1=Kay |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold's heartwarming gesture to help NHS workers at Royal Liverpool hospital |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/trent-alexander-arnolds-brilliant-gesture-18134388 |website=Liverpool Echo |date=22 April 2020 |access-date=22 June 2023 |archive-date=22 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622144227/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/trent-alexander-arnolds-brilliant-gesture-18134388 |url-status=live }}</ref>

He is a supporter of the [[Black Lives Matter]] movement, wearing a special pair of boots featuring the phrase and auctioning them off in a raffle for the [[Nelson Mandela Foundation]], raising £27,000 in the process.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alexander-Arnold |first1=Trent |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold's matchworn signed Black Lives Matter boots |url=https://www.justgiving.com/fundraising/blacklivesmatterboots |website=JustGiving.com |publisher=JustGiving |access-date=9 May 2023 |archive-date=9 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509214711/https://www.justgiving.com/fundraising/blacklivesmatterboots |url-status=live }}</ref> The boots were later displayed in the [[National Football Museum]] in Manchester and [[FIFA Museum]] in Zurich.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold BLM Boots on display at new FIFA exhibition |url=https://www.nationalfootballmuseum.com/news/211-cultures/ |website=National Football Museum |date=10 November 2022 |access-date=9 May 2023 |archive-date=9 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509214718/https://www.nationalfootballmuseum.com/news/211-cultures/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In April 2023, he set up The After Academy, an initiative funded by Alexander-Arnold for the next five years that will support and aide former academy footballers. The After Academy is intended to provide training and career opportunities both in and out of football for footballers who did not make it past academy level and is being run with the co-operation of the PFA and Alexander-Arnold's sponsors, [[Red Bull]], [[Under Armour]] and Therabody.<ref>{{cite web |title=The After Academy: PFA confirmed as supporting partner to Trent Alexander-Arnold's new initiative |url=https://www.thepfa.com/news/2023/4/27/pfa-excited-to-support-trent-alexander-arnolds-after-academy |website=thepfa.com |publisher=Professional Footballers' Association |access-date=9 May 2023 |archive-date=9 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509214718/https://www.thepfa.com/news/2023/4/27/pfa-excited-to-support-trent-alexander-arnolds-after-academy |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Trent Alexander Arnold mural.jpg|thumb|right|Mural of Alexander-Arnold in 2022]]

Alexander-Arnold is the nephew of former [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] and [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] footballer, and former Manchester United club secretary, [[John Alexander (footballer, born 1955)|John Alexander]].<ref name = Uncle>{{cite news |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/liverpool/story/3008300/trent-alexander-arnold-breaks-through-at-liverpool-despite-man-united-family-ties |title=Alexander-Arnold breaks through at Liverpool despite Man United links |first=Mark |last=Ogden |publisher=ESPN |date=30 November 2016 |access-date=27 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528052605/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/liverpool/story/3008300/trent-alexander-arnold-breaks-through-at-liverpool-despite-man-united-family-ties |archive-date=28 May 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> His maternal grandmother, Doreen Carling, was once also in a relationship with former United manager, [[Alex Ferguson]], before moving to New York City where she later married. Alexander-Arnold was thus eligible to play for the United States prior to making his England debut.<ref name=TG>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/02/06/sports/soccer/liverpool-alexander-arnold.html |title=At Global Clubs, Local Players Serve as Connective Tissue |first=Rory |last=Smith |newspaper=The New York Times |date=6 February 2018 |access-date=8 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180208000455/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/02/06/sports/soccer/liverpool-alexander-arnold.html |archive-date=8 February 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> He has two brothers; Tyler, who is four years his senior and acts as his [[Sports agent|agent]], and Marcel, who is three years younger.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-vs-real-madrid-champions-league-trent-alexanderarnold-journey-to-kiev-a8366301.html |title=The making of a man: Trent Alexander-Arnold's journey from Crosby to Kiev |newspaper=The Independent |last=Hughes |first=Simon |date=24 May 2018 |access-date=22 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622083918/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-vs-real-madrid-champions-league-trent-alexanderarnold-journey-to-kiev-a8366301.html |archive-date=22 June 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/01/13/brothers-agents-marcus-rashford-trent-alexander-arnold-robbed/ |title=Brothers and agents of Marcus Rashford and Trent Alexander-Arnold robbed at gunpoint in Moss Side |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |date=13 January 2019 |access-date=14 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114090838/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/01/13/brothers-agents-marcus-rashford-trent-alexander-arnold-robbed/ |archive-date=14 January 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> He is of Scottish and American descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/england-north-macedonia-live-score-updates-result-euro-2024/7nHygHTf1kJx/|title=England's alternative nationalities|first=The|last=Athletic|website=[[The New York Times]] |date=19 June 2023}}</ref>

He is also an avid [[chess]] player, having been introduced to the game by his father as a youngster, and in 2018 he played an invitational match against world champion [[Magnus Carlsen]]. The match, which was played as part of a campaign to promote the sport, ended in defeat for Alexander-Arnold after seventeen moves.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-fc-trent-alexander-arnold-england-magnus-carlsen-chess-world-champion-a8574621.html |title=Trent Alexander-Arnold is outsmarted by the world chess champion, but Liverpool's young buck remains wise beyond his years |newspaper=The Independent |last=Liew |first=Jonathan |date=8 October 2018 |access-date=8 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181009033215/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-fc-trent-alexander-arnold-england-magnus-carlsen-chess-world-champion-a8574621.html |archive-date=9 October 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Alexander-Arnold later explained how chess was more than just a pastime and had helped him in his football career by teaching him to think "two or three moves ahead of the opposition".<ref name=RB/>

Alexander-Arnold is good friends with Real Madrid and England teammate [[Jude Bellingham]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.empireofthekop.com/2025/01/23/trent-alexander-arnold-jude-bellingham-england/ | title=Liverpool fans will wince at what Trent Alexander-Arnold and Jude Bellingham have just done online | date=23 January 2025 }}</ref>

In 2023, Alexander-Arnold joined the investment group of the [[Alpine F1 Team|Alpine racing team]] of [[Formula One]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patrick-mahomes-invests-in-formula-one-team-alpine-ownership|title=Patrick Mahomes invests in Formula One team, 'always looking around' at ownership opportunities|last=Shook|first=Nick|website=NFL.com|date=19 October 2023|access-date=29 November 2023|language=en|archive-date=30 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130231507/https://www.nfl.com/news/patrick-mahomes-invests-in-formula-one-team-alpine-ownership|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/racing/2023/10/17/patrick-mahomes-travis-kelce-investors-alpine-f1-team|title=Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce Become Investors in Alpine F1 Team|publisher=Sports Illustrated|last=McDaniel|first=Mike|date=17 October 2023|access-date=29 November 2023|language=en|archive-date=30 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130184527/https://www.si.com/racing/2023/10/17/patrick-mahomes-travis-kelce-investors-alpine-f1-team|url-status=live}}</ref>
